stem: A compliance requirement spans EBS, RDS, and DynamoDB with one shared retention policy that ages recovery points into cold storage automatically. Select TWO true statements about the solution that meets this. (Select TWO.)

choices.text: AWS Backup can apply one policy across all three resource types
AWS Backup backs up incrementally after the first full backup for supported resources
EBS Snapshot Archive can retain RDS and DynamoDB recovery points under the same policy
S3 Glacier Deep Archive natively manages EBS, RDS, and DynamoDB recovery points
AWS Backup needs a full backup every time, with no incremental option

rationale: AWS Backup centralizes policy-driven backup across many AWS resource types, so one plan can cover EBS, RDS, and DynamoDB together. After the first full backup, AWS Backup backs up incrementally for supported resources, keeping ongoing storage cost tied to changed data. The EBS Snapshot Archive tier is EBS-only, with no mechanism for RDS or DynamoDB recovery points. S3 Glacier Deep Archive stores object data directly; it does not natively manage recovery points from EBS, RDS, or DynamoDB. AWS Backup does not need a full backup every time; incremental backup after the first copy is exactly what keeps its ongoing cost down.
